PullRequest.Title: [1/4] authentication: refresh Copilot on session issuer changes
PullRequest.Body:
## Review stack

**#338149 (1: Copilot identity) → #338150 (2: provider lifecycle) → #338151 (3: credential storage) → #338080 (4: multi-host enablement)**

Each PR targets the preceding branch. Review and merge in numbered order. After squash-merging a layer, rebase and retarget the next layer onto `main` before merging it.

## Stack 1/4: Copilot identity refresh

Base: `main`.

## Review question

Does changing a GitHub session's account or authorization server refresh Copilot authentication and identity-dependent repository state, even when its token and session ID are unchanged?

- Reuse the existing account/issuer comparison when publishing authentication changes.
- Update the code-search subscriber to invalidate repository authorization/index status for the same identity changes, while preserving existing session-ID invalidation.
- Avoid redundant repository refreshes for token-only changes or equivalent session objects.

This is an independent bug fix using the session-provenance API already on main. It adds service and subscriber regressions without changing providers, configuration, credential storage, or enrollment.

## Validation

- 48 targeted authentication/session/code-search tests passing; 1 existing skip.
- Four same-ID account/issuer cases reproduced stale repository status before the subscriber fix; all nine subscriber tests pass afterward.
- Copilot type check, scoped lint, staged hygiene and diff check passed.
- Full-stack follow-up: 105 authentication/code-search/domain/MCP tests passing, 1 existing skip.

The next layer (#338150) separates enterprise registration from host-bound engines while keeping current single-host behavior.
## One-time screenshot baseline acceptance

The maintainer explicitly approved refreshing `sessions/sessionsList/SessionsList_SelectedKeyboardFocus/DarkHighContrast` to the failing CI capture in `c65c3e02bff`. **The maintainer reports that the screenshot difference is not noticeable to their human eye.**

This is a one-time baseline-only exception to this PR's authentication scope: one image hash changed, with no UI or fixture implementation changes. It does not claim to fix the underlying rendering instability.

Scenarios.Scenario: A GitHub authentication session keeps the same token and session ID but changes account ID or authorization server.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The authentication provider event first completes three existing concurrent session lookups, then the diff makes the forced Copilot-token mint complete before publishing onDidAuthenticationChange. Consumers run after that event; most synchronously invalidate bounded caches, while the CLI model subscriber starts an asynchronous model fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queries the any GitHub, permissive GitHub, and ADO authentication sessions concurrently through the authentication API.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three lookups per provider event, coalesced per session lookup key by AuthenticationService TaskSingler when overlapping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same three session lookups already ran for every relevant authentication-provider event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All three settle before identity comparison and token minting.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forces a Copilot token request for the newly detected account/issuer identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One effective request per identity key; concurrent requests for the same provider/account/issuer/access-token key are coalesced by the token manager TaskSingler.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A same-token, same-session-ID account/issuer change did not force a token mint or publish the identity-change event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The authentication-change event is published only after this request settles, but provider-event dispatch itself does not await _handleAuthChangeEvent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The existing authentication-change subscriber eagerly refreshes the available CLI model list through the SDK.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One model-list fetch for the published identity event; a newer event supersedes the stored promise rather than multiplying normal equivalent-session notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This subscriber already fetched on sign-in/sign-out and token-backed identity events, but was not reached for the newly recognized same-token account/issuer case.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Started asynchronously by the event and not awaited by authentication refresh; it does not block publication of the event.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Authentication identity changes, not token refresh frequency: string-value comparisons suppress equivalent reconstructed sessions, and the code-search subscriber also suppresses token-only events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The three session reads run in parallel; token mint follows them and is coalesced per identity. Event listeners fan out synchronously, with their asynchronous work independently scheduled.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Session requests and token minting coalesce concurrent identical keys. Identity-sensitive model, routing, organization, and cloud-session caches are invalidated once; most network reads remain lazy, while CLI models refresh eagerly.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed condition, forced token call, TaskSingler key, and event subscribers are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact authentication-provider event duplication and remote latency vary, but identity changes are infrequent and equivalent-session notifications are explicitly deduplicated.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded one-time network work is tied to a real identity transition and is required to prevent credentials and identity-derived caches from remaining scoped to the previous account or host.

Scenarios.Scenario: Repository authorization/index status refresh after a GitHub session account, issuer, session ID, or sign-out transition.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The authentication event handler snapshots the current two GitHub sessions, compares IDs and account/issuer identity, updates the snapshots before scheduling work, and launches repository refreshes without awaiting them. Code-search consumers may observe CheckingStatus while requests run, but authentication processing is not blocked.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Forces a CAPI remote-index-status GET for every tracked GitHub repository; some not-yet-indexed states may additionally check whether the GitHub repository is empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One status request per tracked GitHub repository/root for one effective identity transition; Promise.all issues them concurrently. Equivalent session objects and token-only changes issue zero requests. There is no cross-root grouping, but realistic cardinality is the number of GitHub repositories tracked in the open workspace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session-ID/sign-out transitions already forced the same per-repository request wave. Same-ID account/issuer transitions previously issued no repository refresh and could retain status authorized for the old identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Requests are fire-and-forget from the authentication event and therefore off the auth critical path; they update later code-search availability.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of tracked GitHub repositories in the workspace after repo tracking; ADO repositories are filtered out. Frequency scales with distinct session/account/issuer transitions, not ordinary token refreshes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All eligible GitHub repository status requests run concurrently via Promise.all with no shared limiter. This is inherited from the existing session-ID refresh path; the diff adds the same behavior only for rare account/issuer identity transitions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: refreshStatusFromEndpoint(true) intentionally bypasses Ready/NotAuthorized short-circuiting because authorization is identity-scoped. The listener stores the latest sessions before scheduling requests, so duplicate equivalent events are negative-cached by equality checks. There is no status-request coalescer across distinct repos.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: force=true, per-repository mapping, GitHub-only filtering, and unbounded Promise.all are directly visible, as are the added identity predicates and token-only suppression test.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large multi-root workspaces can create a wider burst, but typical repository counts are small and the newly added trigger is rare rather than periodic or input-hot.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff adds a bounded refresh only when cached authorization has become identity-invalid; it neither makes token refreshes hit the network nor increases per-transition cardinality beyond the established session-change behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all five changed files and traced the authentication-event expansion through token minting, event subscribers, repository tracking, and remote index-status calls. The added work is bounded to rare account/issuer identity transitions, equivalent sessions and token-only refreshes are suppressed, same-key token work is coalesced, and repository requests are off the authentication critical path. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
